purpose: Reduce actor/geography bias by grounding future propaganda-mechanism coding in primary archival artifacts from multiple countries, eras and conflict roles.

sources.scope: Approximately 1,900 digitized posters, 1914-1920, including US, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Germany, Great Britain, Italy, Netherlands and Russia.
sources.rights: ITEM_LEVEL_RIGHTS; LOC provides rights statements and many items have no known restrictions
sources.defensive_use: cross-country visual mechanism coding and source-controlled historical comparison

sources.institution: Library of Congress Geography and Map Division
sources.collection: 1928 Soviet Russian Civil War pictorial propaganda map series
sources.scope: Ten Soviet pictorial propaganda maps published by the State Publishing House, Military Literature division, narrating Bolshevik victory in the Civil War.
sources.rights: LOC Geography and Map Division digitized content generally free to use/reuse unless a Rights Advisory says otherwise; verify item statement

sources.collection: Powers of Persuasion: Poster Art of World War II
sources.scope: US wartime poster archive/exhibit with catalog identifiers and primary artifacts.
NDL materials include handbills dropped by US Army Air Forces over Japan in 1945 and Japanese bibliographic holdings on wartime propaganda.
sources.rights: NDL item/access terms; metadata may be open while image reuse/access varies
sources.defensive_use: Pacific-war leaflet/psychological-warfare primary context; no operational execution guidance

sources.collection: 大戦ポスター集 / War Posters (1921)
sources.scope: 55 plates plus 122 pages; Japanese bibliographic/digitized record of wartime poster material.
sources.rights: digitized access subject to NDL transmission/access conditions
sources.defensive_use: Japanese archival/bibliographic counterweight; metadata-first unless reuse is cleared

sources.scope: Source-grounded educational corpus on Nazi propaganda, mobilization, persecution and genocide.
sources.rights: USHMM terms; citation/reference unless item reuse is cleared
sources.defensive_use: historical harm and mechanism context, not symmetry-by-moral-equivalence

sources.institution: CIA Reading Room / U.S. Department of State
sources.collection: Soviet Active Measures: Forgery, Disinformation, Political Operations — Special Report No. 88
sources.scope: October 1981 declassified US government assessment of Soviet active measures.
sources.defensive_use: primary institutional assessment with mandatory US-government bias/collection receipt; not exclusive truth

sources.scope: 1980s US intelligence-community records describing alleged front groups, forgeries, media manipulation and influence campaigns.
sources.defensive_use: compare claims across declassified assessments and external scholarship; preserve institutional incentives and unknowns

symmetry_rule: Primary artifacts from one side do not become the moral or factual baseline for another side. Each artifact is coded by the same observable-feature schema, and institutional assessments are never counted as independent confirmation merely because they are declassified.
next_archive_targets: Imperial War Museums multilingual propaganda collections
French and British national archive wartime information collections
Russian/Soviet archival sources where lawful and accessible
Chinese propaganda poster/history archives and scholarship
Japanese home-front primary posters and broadcasts
Global South and decolonization-era primary propaganda corpora
operational_firewall: Archive study is for recognition, historical comparison and defensive countermeasure science; no audience-targeting or deployable influence campaign construction.
